principle_text: When the persuadee expresses general support for charities but has not yet committed to a specific donation, avoid asking only if they have given money without linking to a concrete call to action.
When the persuadee shares general donation preferences, avoid shifting focus prematurely to specific charities without first building relevance to their values and interests.
When the persuadee shows openness and interest, you should positively acknowledge their past contributions and smoothly transition to introducing your specific cause to maintain engagement.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about a charity, avoid assuming prior knowledge or skipping detailed explanations about the charity's goals and impact.
When the persuadee expresses uncertainty about a charity, avoid simply naming it without providing clear, detailed information about its mission and activities.
When the persuadee expresses general positive views about charities, avoid moving too quickly to specific donation requests without first exploring their values and interests in depth.
When the persuadee responds with unrelated or off-topic examples, avoid asking questions that may confuse or derail the conversation from the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses financial limitations, avoid pressing for immediate donations without acknowledging their constraints or exploring alternative ways to contribute.
When the persuadee responds non-committally to an offer of information, avoid vague invitations that do not clearly encourage commitment or express the benefits of engaging further.
When the persuadee expresses strong negative feelings toward a specific charity, avoid introducing that charity directly to prevent resistance and disengagement.

When the persuadee expresses a negative bias toward a charity based on prior statements, avoid asking open-ended questions that may reinforce their resistance without addressing their concerns directly.
When the persuadee expresses a strong negative belief about a charity's impact, avoid simply asking why without addressing their concerns or providing counterarguments.
When the persuadee expresses strong objections to a cause, avoid dismissing their concerns or pressuring them directly, as this can provoke resistance and reduce willingness to engage.
When the persuadee shares their past donation experience, avoid only asking about their actions without linking to emotional or motivational reasons to donate.
